summary: The result is the stored length of the rest-parameter array, so one property read matches the unavoidable constant work needed to return a number.

optimality.argument: Every correct invocation must return one numeric result, establishing an Omega(1) lower bound, while reading args.length performs a fixed property lookup independent of the number or contents of the arguments.

replacement_checks.evidence: Producing the required integer result needs at least one operation.
JavaScript arrays store length, and the reference returns that property without traversing argument values.
Authored cases cover zero arguments, one argument, falsy values, nested containers, mixed types, and the maximum 100 arguments.
